'''Lesley Jane Yellowlees''' (born 1953) is a British [[inorganic chemist]] conducting research in Spectroelectrochemistry, [[Electron transfer|Electron transfer reactions]] and [[Electron paramagnetic resonance|Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) Spectroscopy]]. Yellowlees was also elected as the president of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] 2012–14 and was the first woman to hold that role .<ref name="RSCNews">RSC News, August 2012, pp 12–13 "Lesley Yellowlees"</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1021/ic048799t| pmid = 15651869| title = Synthesis, Structure, and Properties of [Pt(II)(diimine)(dithiolate)] Dyes with 3,3'-, 4,4'-, and 5,5'-Disubstituted Bipyridyl: Applications in Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells| journal = Inorganic Chemistry| volume = 44| issue = 2| pages = 242–50| year = 2005| last1 = Geary | first1 = E. ==Early life and education==
Yellowlees was born in 1953 in [[London]], moving to [[Edinburgh]] at the age of 9 and attending [[St Margaret's School, Edinburgh|St Hilary's Girls' School]]. Her father worked for [[Rank Hovis McDougall]], and she has two sisters.<ref name="Herald">[http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/home-news/youve-got-to-have-support-because-work-isnt-always-going-to-go-well.17824739 ''The Herald'' 2 July 2012] Rebecca McQuilllan "You've got to have support because work is not always going to go well</ref> She completed her higher education at the [[University of Edinburgh]], gaining a BSc in [[Chemical Physics]] in 1975, and PhD in Inorganic [[Electrochemistry]] in 1982. Yellowlees was the only woman graduate in her undergraduate class, graduating with a first.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/nov/03/lesley-yellowlees-solar-energy-research|title=Lesley Yellowlees: 'I saw something no one else had seen'|last=Davis|first=Nicola|date=2013-11-03|work=The Guardian|access-date=2017-11-24|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Continuing on from this Yellowlees began her [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research]] in the [[University of Glasgow]] in 1983.<ref name="yellowphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Lesley |last=Yellowlees |title=Spectro-electrochemical studies on luminescent complexes |publisher=University of Edinburgh |date=1983 |url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/40419054?style=html |id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.664125}} |website=jisc.ac.uk |access-date=13 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215222244/https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/40419054?style=html |archive-date=15 December 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Lesley Yellowlees' first job was as an administrator in the [[National Health Service]], but after moving to [[Brisbane]], she went into electrochemical research<ref name="MRC">[https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20130409142858/http://www.csc.mrc.ac.uk/d/SuffrageContent_web.pdf MRC Clinical Sciences Centre ''Suffrage Science 2013''] 9–13 Lesley Yellowlees and Molly Stevens review successes in science while raising families</ref> subsequently worked in the [[University of Queensland]].  Returning to the University of Edinburgh, to do a PhD on solar cell chemistry, Yellowlees became a demonstrator in 1986, a lecturer in 1989<ref name="Edit">[http://issuu.com/the-university-of-edinburgh/docs/edit-summer-2011 Edit] (University of Edinburgh alumni magazine) June 2011 p 24 "Master and Apprentice"</ref> and was appointed Professor of Inorganic Electrochemistry in 2005. She was the first woman to be appointed head of chemistry in the university.<ref name="MRC" /> And is also [[vice-principal]] of the university and head of the College of Science and Engineering.

===Honours and awards===
[[File:RSC Staircase.jpg|thumb|right|186x186px|A portrait of Prof Yellowlees, by Peter Edwards, hangs on the staircase of the Royal Society of Chemistry.]]
Yellowlees was made a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2005<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2014/Lesley-Yellowlees-CBE.asp|title=Press release: Appointment at the Palace for our president|website=rsc.org|access-date=2019-02-03}}</ref> and an Honorary Fellow of [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/about-us/our-history/our-honorary-fellows/|title=Honorary Fellows of the Royal Society of Chemistry|last=Chemistry|first=Royal Society of|date=2016-06-08|website=rsc.org|language=en|access-date=2019-02-03}}</ref> She became a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2012.<ref name="RSCPLY">[http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/Governance/RSCCouncil/CouncilMembersBiography/lesley-yellowlees.asp Professor Yellowlees]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203021130/http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/Governance/RSCCouncil/CouncilMembersBiography/lesley-yellowlees.asp|date=3 December 2013}}</ref> and is also a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name="Ed">[http://www.ed.ac.uk/schools-departments/science-engineering/about/college-office/profiles/lesley-yellowlees www.ed.ac.uk] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011072122/http://www.ed.ac.uk/schools-departments/science-engineering/about/college-office/profiles/lesley-yellowlees |date=11 October 2014 }} University of Edinburgh "Professor Lesley Yellowlees MBE FRSC FRSE FInstP"</ref>

To mark the [[International Year of Chemistry]], [[IUPAC]] selected 25 women including Yellowlees for the Distinguished Women Chemistry/Chemical Engineering Award.<ref name="IUPAC">[http://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/1310949/Distinguished_Women_ChemistryChemical_Engineering_Award.html www.chemistryviews.org] Distinguished Women Chemistry/Chemical Engineering Award</ref>

She took over the presidency of the Royal Society of Chemistry on 4 July 2012 for a two-year term<ref name="RSCNews" /> (she was succeeded by Professor [[Dominic Tildesley]]).

The [[National Portrait Gallery, London|National Portrait Gallery]] has two portraits of her.<ref name="NPG">{{NPG name | id=61245 |name=Lesley Yellowlees }}</ref><ref name="Jordanova">L. J. Jordanova (2000) Defining Features: Scientific and Medical Portraits, 1660–2000 (Reaktion Books) {{ISBN|1861890591}}</ref> There is also a painting of her by [[Peter Edwards (artist)|Peter Edwards]] in [[Burlington House]], the headquarters of the Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref name="mag">[http://mag.digitalpc.co.uk/olive/ode/rscnews/LandingPage/LandingPage.aspx?href=UlNDTm9kZS8yMDEyLzA4LzAx&pageno=MTI.&entity=QXIwMTIwMA..&view=ZW50aXR5 mag.digitalpc.co.uk] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215090823/http://mag.digitalpc.co.uk/olive/ode/rscnews/LandingPage/LandingPage.aspx?href=UlNDTm9kZS8yMDEyLzA4LzAx&pageno=MTI.&entity=QXIwMTIwMA..&view=ZW50aXR5 |date=15 December 2014 }} Lesley Yellowlees</ref>

Yellowlees was appointed [[Order of the British Empire|MBE]] in 2005 for services to science and [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in the [[2014 New Year Honours]] for services to chemistry.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{London Gazette|issue=60728 |supp=y|page=9|date=31 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/honours-list/10542766/New-Year-Honours-2014-list-in-full.html|title=New Year Honours 2014 |work=The Telegraph newspaper}}</ref>

Yellowlees holds Honorary Doctorates from [[Heriot-Watt University]] (awarded in 2012),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hw.ac.uk/news/archive/2012/summer-graduations-2012.htm |title=Summer Graduations 2012 &#124; News &#124; Heriot-Watt University Edinburgh |access-date=9 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924032041/http://www.hw.ac.uk/news/archive/2012/summer-graduations-2012.htm |archive-date=24 September 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Edinburgh Napier University]] (awarded in 2016).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hazelhall.org/2016/07/07/a-laureation-for-professor-lesley-yellowlees-ednapiergrads/|title=A laureation for Professor Lesley Yellowlees #EdNapierGrads|date=7 July 2016|website=hazelhall.org}}</ref>

Yellowlees was named the [[University of Edinburgh]] Alumnus of the Year 2013 in honour of her research, leadership and her work as an advocate for women in [[STEM fields|STEM subjects]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pioneering scientist named Alumnus of the Year|url=http://www.ed.ac.uk/alumni/services/news/news/alumnus-award|work=ed.ac.uk|publisher=The University of Edinburgh|access-date=29 January 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202113729/http://www.ed.ac.uk/alumni/services/news/news/alumnus-award|archive-date=2 February 2014}}</ref>

In 2014, she was included in the [[100 Women (BBC)|BBC's 100 Women]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-29758792|title=Who are the 100 Women 2014?|publisher=BBC|date=26 October 2014}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She is married to Peter W. Yellowlees, a [[Chartered Accountant]],<ref name="Peter">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130505044355/http://www.merchiston.co.uk/system-pages/footer-menu/governance/governors.aspx|title=Board of Governors, Merchiston School}} P. W. Yellowlees</ref> and they have two children.<ref name="RSCPLY" /><ref name="RSCNews" />
